assertions.name: f1_exact_qd_favard_depth25
assertions.source: exact rational qd algorithm at r = 21/20 (q ~ 1.2155), K = 26: all Jacobi beta_k > 0 for k <= 25 (extends the KSel-2 K3 exact Favard depth 9), beta_1 = qtilde + 1/qtilde - 1 exact, and (M^n)_00 = m_n exact for n <= 12 — the qd route reproduces the canonical operator exactly

assertions.name: f2_deformation_qd_certified
assertions.source: mpf qd at r = 6/5 (q = 2.0736), dps 400, K = 48: beta_k > 0 all k, moment reproduction rel < 1e-300 (measured 8.53e-401), and agreement with the exact-Q qd (K = 12) to rel < 1e-350

assertions.name: f3_friedrichs_limit_positive
assertions.source: r = 6/5: truncation eigenvalues lambda_j(N) strictly decrease in N for every j (polynomials are a form core of the Friedrichs extension => min-max; the truncation limit IS J_F, [simon1998] / [pedersen1995]); lambda_min(48) = 0.336681762134, Cauchy rel 2.07e-7 (N = 42 vs 48): lambda_F in (0.33, 0.34) STRICTLY POSITIVE — the Friedrichs measure has no support near 0

assertions.name: f4_krein_radau_pinned_at_zero
assertions.source: r = 6/5, N = 48 Gauss-Radau truncation with node pinned at 0 (boundary shift t_N = P_N(0)/P_{N-1}(0)) — the canonical solution with 0 in supp = the KREIN extension measure ([pedersen1995]): pinned eigenvalue < 1e-80, all other atoms > 0 and Cauchy (rel < 1e-4), mass at 0 = 1/sum_{k<48} p_k(0)^2 to < 1e-25, sum p_k(0)^2 convergent (indeterminacy corroboration), and the positive Krein atoms INTERLACE the Friedrichs atoms

assertions.name: f5_extremal_grids_q_lattice_u1_class
assertions.source: r = 6/5: Friedrichs atom spacing in qtilde-steps decreases monotonically to 2 (last window value 2.001223) — the extremal supports are asymptotically q-LATTICES, incommensurate with the u-continuum's qtilde-grids; the qtilde-class of the Friedrichs atoms Aitken-extrapolates to 0.805336 vs the u = 1 class phi_1 = 0.805241 (circ dist 9.45e-5; half-shifted class rejected, dist 0.5), and the Krein class extrapolates to 0.805085 (dist 0.000156) — F and K asymptotically occupy complementary q-sublattices of the ONE u = 1 qtilde-grid; the LOW Friedrichs atoms are off that grid (lambda_0 class dist 0.209 > 0.1)

assertions.name: f6_extension_circle_sweep
assertions.source: r = 6/5, N = 44: boundary shifts s*t_N, s in {0, 1/4, 1/2, 3/4, 1} interpolate the truncated extension family — lambda_min strictly decreasing from the Friedrichs value to 0 at the Krein pin (s = 1); at s = 3/2 the smallest eigenvalue is NEGATIVE: boundary conditions beyond Krein leave the Stieltjes (nonnegative) sector of the extension circle

assertions.name: f7_pins_machinery
assertions.source: both q0 pins (muon + proton), K = 24: qd beta_k > 0, moment reproduction < 1e-150, lambda_min(N) strictly decreasing and positive (N = 16/20/24), Radau pin at 0 < 1e-40, Radau mass-at-0 identity < 1e-20. The pins sit deep in the pre-asymptotic window (qtilde - 1 ~ 0.054): asymptotic grid classes are read at the strong-deformation leg (F5), stated as such — no class claim is made at the pins

assertions.name: f8_bar_reflection_no_pushforward_action
assertions.source: (i) sympy exact: sigma: s -> qtilde^{-1}/s fixes the SW factor LN(-L/2, L) and acts on qtilde-grid classes as phi -> -phi with fixed classes exactly {0, 1/2} = the u = 1 / u = qtilde^{1/2} pair (ksel1 R4). (ii) OBSTRUCTION, scope-(b) with cited invariant: every extension measure has smallest positive support point s_min > 0 (discrete spectrum, [simon1998]; lambda_F ~ 0.337 at r = 6/5) or an atom AT 0 (Krein — sigma-image not a finite measure); sigma_* support is then bounded by 1/(qtilde s_min), so its moments grow at most geometrically, while m_{k+1}/m_k is strictly increasing and unbounded (exact) — sigma_* of an extension measure is NEVER a representing measure: the bar reflection does NOT act on the extension circle by pushforward and does NOT exchange Friedrichs and Krein. (iii) numeric: sigma-moment/m_k = 1.43669 (k=1), 0.000124 (k=8) at r = 6/5; 2.88006 (k=1) at r = 21/20

description: KSel-2-ID (bean qou-0ms0; audit-only, NO FIT, nothing wired): Friedrichs/Krein identification for the balanced binding Jacobi operator J(q), by exact-Q + certified-mpf qd Jacobi data, truncation eigenvalues (min-max => Friedrichs limit), and Gauss-Radau-at-0 (=> Krein, the canonical solution with 0 in support, [pedersen1995]). Findings: lambda_F > 0 (strict); Krein has an atom at 0 with mass 1/sum p_k(0)^2; the extremal supports are asymptotically q-lattices (spacing qtilde-steps -> 2), F and K occupying complementary q-sublattices whose common qtilde-class Aitken-extrapolates to the u = 1 class (u-half-step discriminator answered toward u = 1); NONE of the three named kernel candidates (u = 1 grid, qtilde^(1/2) grid, a.c. log-normal) is an extension measure — the u-continuum members are interior Nevanlinna solutions (supports accumulate at 0; extension spectra are discrete with compact resolvent, [simon1998]). Bar reflection: sigma fixes the SW factor and the u-classes {1, qtilde^(1/2)} but does NOT act on the extension circle by pushforward (bounded-support vs superexponential-moment obstruction, scope-(b)); it does NOT exchange Friedrichs and Krein. Extension-circle sweep: boundary conditions interpolate F -> K monotonically; beyond Krein the truncation leaves the nonnegative sector. Pin legs verify positivity + machinery; grid classes are read at the strong-deformation point, stated as such. Nothing here proves or refutes any conjecture.

f4_krein.inf_supp: 0 (atom) — vs Friedrichs inf supp ~ 0.3367: the Friedrichs solution has the LARGEST smallest support point (Pedersen), Krein the smallest

f5_grid.verdict: NONE of the named candidates (u=1 grid, qtilde^(1/2) grid, a.c. log-normal) is Friedrichs or Krein: extension spectra are discrete with no finite accumulation point (compact resolvent, indeterminate case, [simon1998]) and lambda_F > 0, while the u-grids accumulate at 0 and the a.c. kernel is continuous. The u-continuum members are interior (non-extremal) Nevanlinna solutions. NEW STRUCTURE: F/K = complementary q-sublattices asymptotically aligned with the u = 1 class — the extension circle's canonical pair selects the u = 1 class (asymptotic-class sense, measured), answering the KSel-1 half-step discriminator toward u = 1, not qtilde^(1/2).

f8_bar_reflection.fixed_classes: {0, 1/2} mod qtilde^Z = u = 1 and u = qtilde^(1/2) — on the u-CIRCLE (non-canonical solutions), not on the extension circle
